sample.title: Why Is Everyone Leaving New Zealand?
sample.description:
While much of the world thinks of New Zealand as an idyllic redoubt far removed from the world’s problems, one to which many a billionaire has decamped, its working-age population is leaving in record numbers. And many of those emigrating are in their 30s and 40s – professionals with friends and family – rather than college graduates who often return a few years later. 

In this Bloomberg Originals mini-documentary, we explore how successive New Zealand governments have built the world’s most extreme housing market, and how in doing so set the stage for the current exodus. Has stagnant growth and a cost-of-living crisis ended the Kiwi dream – and if so, what can be done to fix it?

sample.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
sample.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

sample.title: US tech stocks rally after dramatic plunge but markets remain shaky | BBC News
sample.description:
US tech stocks have shown signs of a partial recovery after the value of shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms plummeted worldwide.

The drop off came after the Democrats' resounding win in the US midterms, which sparked fears of a reduction in AI development.

On Thursday the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index closed down by more than 5.5%, losing an estimated $2.5tn in market value, according to Dow Jones data.

Businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development, particularly makers of key computer chips and semiconductors, took the hammering. 

Share prices in US markets have edged up on Friday. Chipmaker Nvidia's share price jumped by over 7% and Elon Musk's SpaceX was up 6.19% - though both are yet to recover their heavy losses from yesterday. It's a similar story for chipmakers AMD and Micron.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Faisal Islam.
